raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What changes

This PR adds an opt-in env flag, `SGLANG_SHARE_SCHEDULE_FORWARD_STREAM` (default off). Default behavior does not change.

- **Before:** the overlap scheduler always keeps a separate schedule stream. Every decode step has GPU waits between this stream and the forward stream: the forward stream waits for its inputs, and the WAR barrier makes the schedule stream wait for the forward stream. On ROCm, each stream maps to a different hardware queue. On gfx950, a wait that is pending on one queue slows each kernel dispatch on the busy forward queue. With `SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER=1`, the WAR wait is pending for almost the whole forward step. In our traces this added about 0.6 µs to each forward kernel, or about 1.1 ms per MTP decode step (about 1,860 kernels).
- **After, with the flag set:** the scheduler queues its own GPU work on the forward stream. Both waits are then in order on one stream, so no wait crosses hardware queues. With the coarse WAR barrier, the GPU order is the same as before, because the schedule work already waits for the whole forward. CPU/GPU overlap stays. The flag has no effect with pipeline parallelism.
- **Who sees it:** only servers that set the flag. We measured it on AMD MI355X (gfx950) with GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4, MTP, and the recipe's `SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER=1 SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER=1`.

### Measured

The measurements ran on [salexspb/sglang@a87779a65c](https://github.com/salexspb/sglang/commit/a87779a65c6fe15936f2150c1949ded49a4c96ad) (upstream `e1f43c9a61` plus open GLM-5.3-Flash/HiSparse PRs). The same stream choice was applied at runtime before the event loop starts. The code of this PR is the same logic on current `main`.

Setup: MI355X, GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4 (`OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4`), TP2/EP2, EAGLE 3/1/4 with acceptance forced to 2.99 (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`). HIP runtime: either ROCm/rocm-systems `rocm-7.2.4` or `develop` `d1cf05c0`, loaded into a ROCm 7.2.4 image.

**Steady-state decode** (`python -m sglang.benchmark.one_batch_server`): engine flags `--quantization quark --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --max-running-requests 128 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 96 --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --linear-attn-verify-backend triton --moe-runner-backend aiter --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --disable-radix-cache`, input 32,768 tokens, output 1,024 tokens. Each shape runs twice, and the second run is measured. Metric: `steady_state_output_throughput` (output tok/s). One run per cell.

| HIP runtime | Flag | Batch 8 | Batch 16 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| rocm-systems 7.2.4 | off | 1,244 | 1,930 |
| rocm-systems 7.2.4 | on | 1,329 (+6.9%) | 2,031 (+5.3%) |
| rocm-systems develop | off | 1,236 | 1,932 |
| rocm-systems develop | on | 1,332 (+7.8%) | 2,004 (+3.7%) |

In an earlier round with output 512, the develop runtime without the flag gave 1,919 / 2,847 / 4,016 tok/s at batch 16 / 32 / 64. The flag was not measured at batch 32 and 64.

**AgentX serving** (aiperf AgentX trace replay, 900 s, 10 warmup requests per session, 96 sessions, no client chat template): PD with 1× TP2 prefill and 1× TP2 decode on two nodes (KV over RDMA), rocm-systems `develop` runtime, flag set on the decode engine only. One run each.

| Flag on decode engine | Run | Output tok/s per GPU | Mean ITL (ms) | P90 TTFT (s) | Errors |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| off | A | 611.3 | 13.94 | 15.81 | 0 |
| off | B (earlier) | 603.8 | 14.09 | 15.84 | 0 |
| on | A | 625.4 (+2.3% vs A off) | 13.59 | 17.61 | 0 |

Run A was made the same afternoon on the same two nodes. The two "off" runs differ by 1.2%, so treat the end-to-end gain as about 2–3%.

**AgentX serving, aggregated** (same client): two TP2/EP2 replicas on 4 GPUs behind the router, 180 GB/rank `write_through_selective` HiCache, rocm-systems `rocm-7.2.4` runtime, flag set on both replicas. One run each. Output tok/s per GPU (mean ITL in ms):

| Sessions | Flag off | Flag on |
|---|---:|---:|
| 64 | 472.5 (14.80) | 477.8 (13.92) |
| 96 | 589.1 (23.38); repeat 578.5 (22.72) | 590.7 (21.93) |
| 128 | 561.2 (44.61) | 576.4 (43.72) |

In the aggregated layout, the flag lowers mean ITL by 2–6%, but the throughput change (+0.3% to +2.7%) is near the run-to-run spread (the two flag-off runs at 96 differ by 1.8%). Errors were 0 in all runs.

## Motivation

On gfx950, the cost appears only when a stream waits on an event that is still pending on another, busy hardware queue. ROCm/rocm-systems#12727 hides it in the HIP runtime with a CP pre-wait packet. In our measurements, that pre-wait gives the same decode gain as this flag. This PR gets the gain in SGLang with the stock runtime.

Other options we measured, on the develop runtime:

- `SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER=0` (fine-grained read-done event): no gain (1,235 / 1,925 tok/s at batch 8 / 16). On HIP the read-done event is recorded after the verify graph replay, so it is still pending for most of the step.
- `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1`: most of the gain (1,323 / 2,008 tok/s). But it puts every stream in the process on one hardware queue.
- `--disable-overlap-schedule` also uses one stream, but it removes CPU/GPU overlap. It was not measured.

## Modifications

- `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_SHARE_SCHEDULE_FORWARD_STREAM = EnvBool(False)`.
- `managers/utils.py`: add `select_schedule_stream()`. It returns the forward stream when sharing is on. Otherwise it keeps the existing behavior: a schedule stream distinct from the forward stream, redrawn if it aliases.
- `managers/scheduler.py`: `run_event_loop` uses the helper. Sharing applies only when the flag is set and `pp_size == 1`. The choice happens before `StreamContext(self.schedule_stream)` and `dispatch_event_loop`, so every event loop (including PD decode) and every component that reads `scheduler.schedule_stream` or the current stream sees the shared stream.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_select_schedule_stream.py`: CPU unit test for the default, the alias redraw, the shared case, and the flag default.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy run. The flag changes only the stream on which the scheduler's GPU work is queued. With the coarse WAR barrier, the GPU order is the same. All measured runs finished with 0 errors.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See **Measured** above. Torch profiler traces of the develop runtime show two `hipStreamWaitEvent` calls per decode step: `Scheduler._apply_war_barrier` and the forward-input wait in `run_batch`. The forward stream is never idle, and its kernels run longer: the median matched kernel takes 0.6 µs more than with the pre-wait runtime.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (speed only; see Accuracy Tests) according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -651,6 +651,13 @@ class Envs:
     # Force the WAR barrier to wait for the whole forward instead of the
     # read-done fastpath event.
     SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER = EnvBool(False)
+    # Overlap scheduler: queue the scheduler's own GPU work on the forward stream
+    # instead of a separate schedule stream. The schedule/forward stream waits
+    # then stay in order on one stream rather than crossing hardware queues.
+    # Scheduler GPU work no longer overlaps the forward on the GPU; with the
+    # coarse WAR barrier it already waits for the whole forward. Ignored with
+    # pipeline parallelism.
+    SGLANG_SHARE_SCHEDULE_FORWARD_STREAM = EnvBool(False)
     # Enable prefill read-done publication after compliant metadata initialization.
     SGLANG_ENABLE_PREFILL_WAR_READ_DONE = EnvBool(False)
     # PP: skip output send/recv when the entire batch consists of non-final chunked prefill requests,

@@ -286,8 +286,8 @@
 from sglang.srt.managers.utils import (
     EmbeddingBatchResult,
     GenerationBatchResult,
-    allocate_distinct_stream,
     is_health_check_generate_req,
+    select_schedule_stream,
     validate_input_length,
 )
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache import kv_cache_builder
@@ -1910,12 +1910,21 @@ def run_event_loop(self) -> None:
         ):
             # CUDA/HIP streams come from a fixed round-robin pool. Redraw if this
             # stream aliases forward_stream, which would eliminate scheduler
-            # overlap. Only CUDA/HIP streams expose a ``cuda_stream`` handle;
+            # overlap, unless SGLANG_SHARE_SCHEDULE_FORWARD_STREAM asks for one
+            # stream. Only CUDA/HIP streams expose a ``cuda_stream`` handle;
             # other accelerators (e.g. NPU/XPU) skip the alias check.
-            if self.schedule_stream.cuda_stream == self.forward_stream.cuda_stream:
-                self.schedule_stream = allocate_distinct_stream(
-                    self.device_module, (self.forward_stream,)
-                )
+            share_forward_stream = (
+                envs.SGLANG_SHARE_SCHEDULE_FORWARD_STREAM.get()
+                and get_parallel().pp_size == 1
+            )
+            if share_forward_stream:
+                logger.info("Scheduler GPU work shares the forward stream.")
+            self.schedule_stream = select_schedule_stream(
+                self.device_module,
+                self.schedule_stream,
+                self.forward_stream,
+                share_forward_stream=share_forward_stream,
+            )
         # The global WAR barrier fences the scheduler's next shared-buffer write
         # on the previous forward's read of the unified memory pool.
         self._war_barrier_enabled = is_cuda() or envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER.get()

@@ -47,6 +47,22 @@ def allocate_distinct_stream(device_module, avoid_streams):
     raise RuntimeError("Unable to allocate a distinct stream")
 
 
+def select_schedule_stream(
+    device_module, schedule_stream, forward_stream, share_forward_stream: bool
+):
+    """The stream the overlap scheduler queues its own GPU work on.
+
+    By default a stream distinct from ``forward_stream``, so the scheduler's GPU
+    work can overlap the forward. With ``share_forward_stream``, ``forward_stream``
+    itself, so every schedule/forward wait stays in order on one stream.
+    """
+    if share_forward_stream:
+        return forward_stream
+    if schedule_stream.cuda_stream == forward_stream.cuda_stream:
+        return allocate_distinct_stream(device_module, (forward_stream,))
+    return schedule_stream
+

 @dataclasses.dataclass
 class GenerationBatchResult:

+"""The overlap scheduler's schedule stream: distinct from the forward stream
+by default, the forward stream itself with SGLANG_SHARE_SCHEDULE_FORWARD_STREAM."""
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.managers.utils import select_schedule_stream
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=1, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _FakeDeviceModule:
+    """Hands out streams from a fixed handle sequence, like a round-robin pool."""
+
+    def __init__(self, handles):
+        self._handles = itertools.cycle(handles)
+        self.drawn = 0
+
+    def Stream(self, priority=0):
+        self.drawn += 1
+        return SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=next(self._handles))
+
+
+class TestSelectScheduleStream(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_keeps_a_distinct_schedule_stream(self):
+        device = _FakeDeviceModule([3])
+        schedule, forward = (
+            SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=2),
+            SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=1),
+        )
+        chosen = select_schedule_stream(
+            device, schedule, forward, share_forward_stream=False
+        )
+        self.assertIs(chosen, schedule)
+        self.assertEqual(device.drawn, 0)
+
+    def test_redraws_an_aliasing_schedule_stream(self):
+        device = _FakeDeviceModule([1, 1, 4])
+        schedule, forward = (
+            SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=1),
+            SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=1),
+        )
+        chosen = select_schedule_stream(
+            device, schedule, forward, share_forward_stream=False
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(chosen.cuda_stream, 4)
+        self.assertEqual(device.drawn, 3)
+
+    def test_shares_the_forward_stream_when_asked(self):
+        device = _FakeDeviceModule([3])
+        schedule, forward = (
+            SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=2),
+            SimpleNamespace(cuda_stream=1),
+        )
+        chosen = select_schedule_stream(
+            device, schedule, forward, share_forward_stream=True
+        )
+        self.assertIs(chosen, forward)
+        self.assertEqual(device.drawn, 0)
+
+    def test_sharing_is_off_by_default(self):
+        self.assertFalse(envs.SGLANG_SHARE_SCHEDULE_FORWARD_STREAM.get())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
